sample.title: Neye yatırım yapıyoruz?
sample.text: Bir veri merkezine ilk kez giren bir yatırımcının gördüğü şey genellikle kabinetlerdir. Sıralar halinde duran siyah kabinetler, içlerindeki sunucular, yanıp sönen ışıklar ve kilometrelerce kablo. Fakat veri merkezinin kendisi bunların hiçbiri değildir. Kabinet, yalnızca görünen son noktadır. Asıl yatırım; o kabinetin yılın üç yüz altmış beş günü, günün yirmi dört saati güvenilir biçimde çalışabilmesini sağlayan bütün sistemdir. Elektriktir. Soğutmadır. Fiber bağlantıdır. Fiziksel güvenliktir. Siber güvenliktir. İzlemedir. Operasyondur. Bakımdır. Prosedürdür. İnsan kaynağıdır. Ve bütün bunların tek bir yapı gibi davranmasını sağlayan mühendislik disiplinidir.

profiles.name: Sage Baseline
profiles.instructions: Speak in Turkish as a highly experienced infrastructure strategist. Prioritize clarity, technical articulation and confidence over drama. Target roughly 130 to 135 words per minute. Neutral, composed and analytical. Use subtle emphasis on investment conclusions and engineering terms. English technical terminology should remain crisp. No casual podcast style, no enthusiasm padding, no promotional tone.

profiles.name: Sage Warm Executive
profiles.instructions: Speak in Turkish as a senior data-center adviser briefing an investor in person. Keep the technical clarity of an experienced engineer, but sound more natural, warm and human than a synthesized narration. Calm and confident, with a comfortable conversational cadence while remaining formal. Avoid metallic cadence, over-precise syllable timing, radio-announcer energy, theatrical pauses or sales tone. Use short natural pauses only where meaning requires them. Target about 130 words per minute. Keep Turkish pronunciation fluent and native-sounding; pronounce established English technical terms clearly and naturally.

profiles.name: Sage Senior Adviser
profiles.instructions: Speak in Turkish as a seasoned technical adviser presenting a high-value infrastructure investment to a board-level investor. Authoritative without sounding stern, mature without sounding slow. Natural human phrasing, restrained warmth and clear reasoning. Allow important conclusions to land with brief pauses, but maintain forward momentum. Avoid metallic or robotic rhythm, exaggerated documentary delivery, advertising tone and podcast casualness. Target roughly 127 to 132 words per minute. Technical English terminology should be crisp but integrated naturally into Turkish speech.

manual_checks: Turkish pronunciation sounds native enough for investor use
Voice sounds natural rather than metallic or synthetic
Credibility as a senior technical adviser
No casual podcast, advertising or radio-announcer tone
Voice remains comfortable for 45–55 minutes of continuous briefing
